learningObjective: Compare the per-rank bandwidth costs of ring-AllGather, ring-ReduceScatter and ring-AllReduce and the relationships between them.
stem: For a total payload of S bytes on N ranks arranged as a ring, ignoring the latency term α, which THREE of the following statements about per-rank bandwidth cost are correct?

options.text: Ring-AllReduce cost equals the sum of ring-ReduceScatter and ring-AllGather, i.e. 2·(N-1)/N · S per rank.
Ring-AllGather per rank must move N · S bytes because every rank has to see every other rank's full copy of the payload.
Ring-AllGather per rank sends and receives (N-1)/N · S bytes (each rank starts with its own S/N shard and must receive the remaining (N-1)·(S/N)).
Ring-ReduceScatter per rank moves (N-1)/N · S bytes, matching AllGather's per-rank cost.

explanation: A, B, C are the standard ring-collective costs. AllGather receives S − S/N = (N-1)/N · S per rank. ReduceScatter on a ring pipelines partial reductions with the same per-rank byte movement, (N-1)/N · S. AllReduce = ReduceScatter + AllGather = 2·(N-1)/N · S per rank. D is wrong: no rank ends with N·S bytes; every rank ends with S bytes (the whole payload once).

optionExplanations.A: Correct: sum of the two phases.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: overcounts by a factor N (confuses per-hop volume with per-rank end state).
optionExplanations.C: Correct: canonical AllGather cost on a ring.

assumptions: The ring implementation is used (no tree/hypercube).
Latency term α is negligible relative to the bandwidth term.
S is evenly divisible by N.
nonImplications: Does not imply the same equalities on hypercube/tree topologies.
Does not imply the wall-clock cost is exactly (N-1)/N · S / BW; contention and pipelining stalls can push it higher.

sourceRefs.locator: Ch. 6 cost analysis of ring collectives

performanceClaim.scope: Ring collectives on N ranks with payload S
